answer_1.quote: We propose DetoxLLM, the first end-to-end framework for the detoxification task ... Given a toxic text, our detoxification model will first analyze and provide an explanation as to why the input is found toxic. Then, the model will attempt to detoxify and output the non-toxic version of the input.
answer_1.outputs: non‑toxic version of the input together with a toxicity explanation

answer_2.quote: We evaluate the models based on six metrics: Accuracy, BERTScore, Content Similarity, Fluency, Joint Metric, BLEU.

answer_4.quote: We conduct a human evaluation framework ... we implement a four-level (A, B, C, D) rating system to measure the detoxification responses from the model. ... Two pairs of fluent English speakers (total=4) voluntarily rate the samples ... each test sample is rated by two evaluators.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rate each model output using a four‑level scale (A: best, B, C, D: worst) based on relevance, meaning preservation, fluency and toxicity; for non‑detoxifiable inputs they use additional N/T ratings.
